_about: Clarification question bank for personalised web-task decisions. Each decision (pick the site, or pick a value for a vague slot) is preceded by yes/no questions answered by Jev from the user's history. Slot types were mined from the vague phrases in the 150 level-1 intents only (no ground-truth values used). Three question kinds: facet = what shape the user's value has (does it include X?), hypothesis = is this candidate the user's value (one per candidate), contrast = is this candidate better supported than a rival. {slot} = the vague phrase, {cand} = a candidate value, {task} = the task.

site.description: Which website the task should be completed on
hypothesis: Has the user done this kind of task ({task}) on {cand} before?
Has the user completed a purchase, booking, or reservation on {cand} for this kind of item or activity?
Has the user used {cand} more than once for this kind of item or activity?
Is {cand} the site the user uses most recently for this kind of item or activity?
negative: Is {cand} only a search engine, map, review aggregator, or general portal that the user uses on the way to another site, rather than where the task gets done?
Is {cand} a site the user associates with a different kind of item or activity than this task?

location.description: City, area, neighbourhood, address, or airport
facet: Does the user consistently refer to a single city for this kind of activity?
Does the user refer to a specific neighbourhood or district rather than just a city?
Does the user use an airport code or airport name?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the location the user usually means for this kind of activity?
Does the user mention {cand} more than once in their history?

budget.description: Price cap, budget, price range, or per-unit price
facet: Is the user's budget expressed per person or per ticket rather than as a total?
Is the user's budget expressed per unit (per dozen, per pod, per night) rather than as a total?
Does the user give a price range (minimum and maximum) rather than a single cap?
Does the user's budget differ by item category, so the category matters here?
Does the user prefer free or low-cost options rather than a specific dollar amount?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the user's usual budget for this kind of item or activity?
Has the user repeatedly stayed within {cand} for this kind of item or activity?

rating.description: Minimum star rating, critic score, review standard
facet: Does the user's rating standard also require a minimum number of reviews?
Does the user express the standard as a plus threshold (for example 4.3+), rather than an exact value?
Does the user use a percentage or critic score rather than stars?
Does the user require the rating to be visible or verified?
Is the user's threshold different for this category than for others?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the user's usual rating standard for this kind of item or activity?
Does the user apply {cand} consistently across several searches?

facet: Does the user specify two measurements together (for example waist by inseam like 32x32)?
Does the user use letter sizes (S, M, L) rather than numeric sizes?
Does the user specify a fit (slim, regular, wide) alongside the size?
Does the user's size include a gender or department label (men's, women's)?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the size the user usually buys for this kind of item?
Has the user bought {cand} more than once?

facet: Does the user's party size depend on the occasion (family, colleagues, date)?
Does the user describe the booking as a table for a number of people?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the party size the user usually books for this kind of occasion?

time.description: Time window, date pattern, edition or release year
facet: Does the user specify a time range (start and end) rather than a single time?
Does the user have more than one regular time window (for example morning and evening)?
Does the user use a 'this year or newer' style cutoff (for example 2020+)?
Does the user state a duration or weekly hour commitment?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the time pattern the user usually means for this kind of activity?

category.description: Genre, cuisine, topic, interest, occupation, tour type, nutrition focus
facet: Does the user have more than one preferred category here (for example two genres or cuisines)?
Does the user narrow the category by era, sub-style, or qualifier (for example 2000s indie, small-business bookkeeping)?
Is the user's preference here an exclusion or restriction (for example allergen-free, gluten-free)?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the user's preferred category for this kind of activity?
Does the user return to {cand} repeatedly?

named_entity.description: Specific restaurant, brand, artist, team, theater, seller, or product
facet: Does the user name one specific place, brand, or person for this repeatedly?
Does the user's preferred item include a qualifier (for example cage-free large, organic, unsweetened)?
Does the user include the location or branch along with the name (for example Uchi Denver)?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the specific one the user means?
Has the user visited, booked, or bought {cand} more than once?

attributes.description: Specs, materials, format, condition, class, seating, amenities, sort or filter habits, delivery options
facet: Does the user's preference combine several attributes together (for example size, resolution, refresh rate, and price)?
Does the user have a habitual sort order or filter they apply on this site?
Does the user accept alternatives (for example open-box or refurbished, paperback or hardcover)?
Does the user list two acceptable options joined by 'or' (for example Dolby Cinema or IMAX)?
hypothesis: Is {cand} the user's usual preference for this attribute?
Has the user chosen {cand} more than once?
